topic: the Harvard Houghton Library book bound in human skin (Des destinées de l'âme), confirmed real via 2014 peptide testing, and its 2024 removal
title: Harvard's Human-Skin Book Was Real, Then They Quietly Took It Apart
description: AI-narrated commentary on the real human-skin book Harvard's library once held — how scientists confirmed it, and why the university took it apart in 2024. Sources below.

hook_candidates.text: A real Harvard library book was bound in human skin, and it's not an urban legend.
A French doctor once bound a book using skin taken from a dead woman's body.
What do you do after finding out your library's book is bound in human skin?
In the 1860s, a med student stole skin from a corpse to bind his friend's book.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists every human skin book story online is an urban legend, because they want to prove Harvard actually had a real one and quietly took it apart.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume a real human skin book is just an urban legend, not something Harvard actually owned and later took apart.
closing_comment: Harvard's own human-skin book was one of only eighteen ever confirmed real, and it still didn't survive intact. What's the darkest true history fact you know?
